demo_trqa_001: Provinces of Oskeria. Oskeria is divided into five provinces: Velmar, Ardunia, Corran, Brannoch and Vardequist. Velmar, Brannoch and Vardequist have a coastline on the Gulf of Amberly; Ardunia and Corran are landlocked.
demo_trqa_002: Velmar province, which contains the capital Velmaran, covers 1,240 square kilometres and is the most densely settled part of the island.
demo_trqa_003: Brannoch province covers 2,310 square kilometres, much of it marshland drained in the 1890s.
demo_trqa_004: Vardequist province, at the island's western tip, covers 860 square kilometres of moor and cliff.
demo_trqa_005: Ardunia province covers 3,050 square kilometres of farmland along the Ardune and is the largest province of Oskeria.
demo_trqa_006: Lighthouses of Oskeria. Four working lighthouses guide ships around the island today: Cape Vardequist, Port Ilse, Hadley Point and the Selm estuary light.
demo_trqa_007: The Cape Vardequist lighthouse was first lit in 1868. Its stone tower stands 31 metres tall.
demo_trqa_008: The Port Ilse light was first lit in 1902; its iron tower is 24 metres high.
demo_trqa_009: Hadley Point lighthouse, first lit in 1911, is a squat tower 40 feet high.
demo_trqa_010: The Selm estuary light was first lit in 1955 and rises 18 metres above the dunes.
demo_trqa_011: Morrow Rock lighthouse was first lit in 1879 and guided ships past the rock until it was decommissioned in 1931.
demo_trqa_012: The Ardune is the longest river of Oskeria, 46 kilometres from its source in the Morrowfen hills to the sea at Port Ilse.
demo_trqa_013: The Varrow is the shorter of the two rivers that rise in the Morrowfen hills; it flows south through the Brannoch marshes.
demo_trqa_014: The Kell drains the eastern moors of Oskeria and is 24 kilometres long, which makes it one of the island's rivers longer than twenty kilometres.
demo_trqa_015: Three bridges cross the Ardune in Velmaran: the Assembly Bridge, the Mill Bridge and the Quay Bridge.
demo_trqa_016: The Mill Bridge in Velmaran was rebuilt in stone after the flood of 1911.
demo_trqa_017: Velmaran's Quay Bridge carries the tram line to Port Ilse; it was repaired after the flood.
demo_trqa_018: Birds of the Brannoch marshes. Thirteen species have been recorded in the marshes: the Brannoch heron, the Amberly egret, the marsh bittern, the Oskerian reed warbler, the Varrow kingfisher, the grey crake, the dune plover, the moor harrier, the sedge bunting, the black-tailed rail, the Morrowfen teal, the lesser marsh tern and the Selm grebe.
demo_trqa_019: The Brannoch heron and the Amberly egret nest in the reed beds of the Brannoch marshes every spring.
demo_trqa_020: The Vardequist scops owl is found only on the cliffs of western Oskeria.
demo_trqa_021: The Morrowfen wood owl, a large brown owl, lives in the old forests of the Morrowfen hills.
